content_units: Brisbane Split-System Triage

For a 2-bedroom,   82 m²   rental,   uneven cooling + water dripping after  30 minutes   most often points to a   dirty filter, blocked condensate drain, poor airflow, or installation/drainage slope issue  . Refrigerant is possible, but it is   less likely to be the first DIY conclusion   unless cooling is clearly weak even with clean airflow.
Likely order to check:
-   1) Filter / airflow issue   — common, low-cost, safe to inspect
-   2) Drain blockage   — very common when dripping starts after running
-   3) Installation / leveling / drain hose routing issue   — possible if problem is recurring
-   4) Refrigerant issue   — technician-only, especially if icing or poor cooling is present
Rental AC Fault Checklist
Step   Action   What to Check   Expected Result
1   Turn unit off and inspect filters   Dust buildup, lint, visible clogging behind front cover   Filters should look mostly open, not grey/matted
2   Check mode and setpoint   Use   Cool   mode, fan medium/high, temp around 22–24°C   Stable cooling without short cycling
3   Inspect airflow at indoor head   Weak output, blocked louvers, furniture/curtains restricting circulation   Strong, even airflow across room
4   Look for water pattern   Drips from front panel/underside vs. outdoor drain point   Water should exit via drain, not from indoor unit
5   Check for ice or frost   Ice on coils, copper lines, or unusual condensation   No ice should be visible
6   Smell and listen   Gurgling is sometimes normal; hissing, buzzing, musty odor are not   Normal fan/compressor sound, no strong odor
7   Inspect visible drain path only   Kinked hose, obvious sag, disconnected outlet near outdoor area   Drain route should be unobstructed and sloped
8   Escalate if still dripping   Continued leak after filter clean and restart   Landlord/technician should arrange repair
What the Tenant Can Safely Inspect
Option 1:   Filters and return airflow     Most likely simple cause     Low-cost first check
- Open the indoor unit cover and remove the   mesh filters   if they are user-removable.
- If dusty, wash gently with lukewarm water, dry fully, then reinstall.
- Run the unit again for 30–60 minutes.
- If cooling improves and dripping stops, this was likely an   airflow/condensation   problem.
Option 2:   Thermostat and operating mode     Rules out settings issue     Safe to verify
- Confirm it is on   Cool  , not Dry/Fan/Auto if behavior seems odd.
- Set fan to   medium or high   temporarily.
- Close windows/doors and check whether one room is much warmer due to sun exposure rather than AC fault.
Option 3:   Visible indoor leak pattern     Helps identify drain vs coil issue     Safe visual inspection
- Put a towel/container under the drip point.
- Note whether water appears only after 20–40 minutes.
- If the drip comes from the   front edge or casing  , that often suggests   drainage backup, poor leveling, or coil icing/overflow  .
Option 4:   Visible outdoor drain discharge     Confirms condensate is leaving properly     Safe external check
- If accessible from a balcony/yard, see whether water is draining outside while cooling.
- No outside drainage plus indoor dripping often points to a   blocked drain line  .
- Do   not   dismantle piping covers or force-clean hidden tubing in a rental.
What Needs a Licensed Technician
Option 1:   Drain line clearing beyond basic visible checks     Likely if indoor dripping persists     Usually service-call level
Arrange repair
- Deep condensate blockage inside the tray/line
- Indoor unit needing partial disassembly
- Persistent leak despite clean filters and correct settings
Option 2:   Refrigerant diagnosis     Not tenant-safe     Licensed AC tech only
- Signs include   poor cooling, icing, hissing, longer run times
- Refrigerant handling in Australia requires a properly licensed technician
- This is   not   a DIY top-up situation
Option 3:   Installation fault or poor unit leveling     Common in recurring leak cases     Technician/installer issue
- Improper fall on drain line
- Indoor unit mounted slightly off-level
- Drain hose trapped, kinked, or incorrectly routed in wall cavity
When to Contact the Landlord Immediately
Contact the landlord/property manager   right away   if any of these apply:
-   Water is leaking onto walls, flooring, power points, or furniture
- The unit   keeps dripping after filter cleaning and a short retest
- You see   ice/frost   on the indoor unit or pipes
- Cooling is   clearly weak in the whole apartment  , not just one room
- There is a   burning smell, electrical smell, buzzing, or tripping breaker
- The leak is recurring and appears to be from the   casing/front panel  , not normal drain discharge
- The unit is the main fixed cooling for the rental and is not functioning properly
For a rental, this is usually the best sequence:
- Clean/inspect filters
- Photograph the leak and note when it starts
- Send the landlord/property manager a short fault report the same day if dripping continues
Likely Cause and Cost Outlook
Based on your symptoms, the most likely causes are:
-   Dirty filter / airflow restriction   — often   AUD 0–30   if tenant-cleanable
-   Blocked condensate drain   — often   AUD 120–250   for a basic service call
-   Installation/drain slope issue   — may exceed   AUD 250   depending on access
-   Refrigerant leak/fault   — often   above AUD 250  , especially if leak-testing/repair/regas is needed
For your   AUD 250   budget, the most realistic “simple fix” range is:
-   Filter clean
-   Basic drain clean/service
-   Minor maintenance call
A refrigerant or installation correction is more likely to become a   landlord repair matter  , not a tenant-paid quick fix.
